The SciML Frontiers 2026 workshop will take place at building W of the University of Augsburg, Germany.

All scheduled talks and plenary sessions will be held in lecture hall T.B.D. (room T.B.D.). Four adjacent seminar rooms (T.B.D. – T.B.D.) will host the breakout sessions. The foyer of Building W will serve as the catering area for lunch and coffee breaks.

## Evening activities

Die Tafeldecker in der Fuggerei\
Jakoberstraße 26\
86152 Augsburg\
Germany

### About the Fuggerei

The [Fuggerei](https://www.fugger.de/en/fuggerei) is the oldest social housing complex in the world still in use. It was
founded in 1521 by the Augsburg merchant and banker Jakob Fugger "the Rich" as a settlement for citizens of Augsburg who
had fallen into need through no fault of their own. Today it consists of 67 houses with 142 apartments, together with its
own church and administrative buildings, enclosed by a wall with gates that are still locked at night.

Remarkably, the rent has never been raised in more than 500 years: residents pay one Rhenish guilder per year — today
€0.88 — plus a daily commitment to three prayers for the founder and his family. Around 150 people live there under these
conditions. Several small museums on the grounds document the founding of the settlement, everyday life in it today, and
its destruction during the Second World War.

### Getting there by tram

**From the workshop venue:** take tram line **3** towards *Augsburg Hauptbahnhof* from the stop **Innovationspark/LfU**
(about a 3-minute walk east of Building W) to **Königsplatz**, then change to tram line **1** towards *Lechhausen Neuer
Ostfriedhof* and get off at the stop **Fuggerei**. The main entrance is directly at the stop.

**From the city centre or the main station:** any tram or bus to **Königsplatz**, then line **1** towards *Lechhausen
Neuer Ostfriedhof* to **Fuggerei**. The Fuggerei is also only a few minutes' walk from the city centre.
